official_sources.title: GDALRasterBand data type, scale, offset and nodata semantics
official_sources.finding: Band datatype, raw nodata, scale, offset and mask semantics are explicit; RasterIO performs datatype translation but does not automatically apply scale/offset.

official_sources.title: GDAL PAM scale-offset semantics
official_sources.finding: Physical units equal raw*scale+offset and applying scale/offset is the caller's responsibility.

official_sources.title: GDAL GeoTIFF driver numeric storage options
official_sources.finding: GeoTIFF supports multiple datatypes, compression modes, predictors, NBITS and lossy options whose settings can affect stored numeric fidelity.

official_sources.title: GeoTIFF DISCARD_LSB behavior
official_sources.finding: DISCARD_LSB explicitly clears least-significant bits and is lossy; terminal terrain storage must reject it.

official_sources.title: GeoTIFF LERC MAX_Z_ERROR
official_sources.finding: LERC MAX_Z_ERROR defaults to 0 for lossless operation; positive thresholds permit bounded lossy value error.

official_sources.title: GeoTIFF NBITS reduced precision
official_sources.finding: NBITS can reduce effective integer precision or create Float16 storage from Float32; terminal DTM identity must pin bit depth.

official_sources.title: GDAL RFC15 band masks
official_sources.finding: GDAL masks encode invalid pixels separately from numeric values, with zero invalid and nonzero valid.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster data model
official_sources.finding: Raster bands may expose nodata, masks, datatype, scale, offset, units and exact/approximate statistics as distinct metadata concepts.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster info metadata inventory
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info reports datatype, nodata, masks and other band metadata needed for immutable numeric-read manifests.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate strict datatype conversion
official_sources.finding: Strict mode can fail instead of silently allowing information-losing datatype conversion; scale/unscale and resampling are separate operations.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster unscale
official_sources.finding: Unscale computes raw*scale+offset and can default many input types to Float32 output, so output datatype must be explicitly audited.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster scale
official_sources.finding: Scaling can clip or transform source values and is not generally invertible after lossy/nonlinear processing.

official_sources.title: GDAL VRT unscale option
official_sources.finding: VRT can apply unscale and output datatype choices virtually, so derived VRT semantics must not be mistaken for raw source values.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster compare golden checks
official_sources.finding: Raster compare checks datatype, nodata, pixels and optional metadata/binary identity against a golden reference.

official_sources.title: NumPy floating point machine limits
official_sources.finding: finfo exposes bit width and epsilon for floating datatypes; representable spacing depends on datatype and magnitude.

official_sources.title: NumPy adjacent-float spacing
official_sources.finding: spacing and nextafter expose adjacent representable floating values and support ULP-level replay QA.

official_sources.title: NumPy safe casting policy
official_sources.finding: safe casting is defined as preserving values; float64 to float32 is not generally a safe cast.

official_sources.title: NumPy exact array equality
official_sources.finding: array_equal requires identical shape and elements, unlike tolerance-based comparisons.

official_sources.title: NumPy tolerance comparison caveats
official_sources.finding: allclose uses explicit atol/rtol and can accept unequal values; default tolerances are not appropriate for every magnitude.

official_sources.title: NumPy ULP assertion
official_sources.finding: assert_array_max_ulp measures differences in units in the last place and supports deterministic floating-point replay checks.
